Really fun rougelite FPS to play with friends, though when playing solo some of the issues of this game get laid bare. Scrolls can be a bit boring in how they boost your abilities, mostly just being stat boosts you get outright or if you do something simple. Ascensions are pretty simple too, but their boosts are often large enough to see the difference in cooldown, damage, or your other stats. I've liked playing all of the characters the game offers so far, their unique abilities end up having you play very differently and focus on different weapon types per character. Bosses are OK, most are simple fights where you can learn their attacks, while others have a gimmick to their fights, and one is a DPS CHECK (this alone has killed so many of my runs).

Now that the game is out of Early Access there's so much more to do compared to when I started playing years ago. The new Spiritual Assault gamemode is really fun, and there's more bosses and paths to take. If you are willing to learn common synergies and have a group to play it with. It's very hard the further you get into a run, and it can feel frustrating when you get one-tapped by an attack that just barely clipped you, which is why I say that the game feels less frustrating when played as a group.
Seriously one of the better chill co-op experiences available on steam now!

Gunfire Reborn is like a roguelike Borderlands. You pick one of the heroes for a 30-60m run through 3-4 acts. Each act has its own style, collection of enemies, and two possible boss fights. Along the way you gain levels that give you perks, collect "occult scrolls" that give you more perks, and pick up weapons with different elements and very different firing properties. Successful runs unlock higher difficulties, and between runs you can unlock permanent buffs or new characters.
The gameplay variety is incredible. Weapons are wildly different- melee weapons, tracking weapons, richocheting weapons, grenade and rocket launchers, flamethrowers, reflectors, anything you can imagine. Each character, too, has very different action skills and grenades, which can become even more distinct with the right perks. The right occult scrolls can completely change your run, too, eg by making you near invulnerable at range but frail up close.
The enemies are distinct but straightforward. They pretty much each have one thing they do: there's the sniper enemies you take cover from, the summoner enemies you go after first, the tank enemies who try to get in your way, etc. They're vanilla but that works well as a foil for the PCs. You're the Harlem Globetrotters and they're the Washington Generals.
The graphics and sound are the same. They serve the gameplay well but are unremarkable. It's easy to tell what you're fighting and there aren't a ton of effects getting in the way.
I don't think it's infinitely replayable - you can unlock all the permanent bonuses and difficulty levels in a few dozen hours, and the limitless modes aren't that appealing. I've gotten more than a hundred hours of fun from it though and I'm not done yet.
